prompt: Finance exports sales from a spreadsheet; data/revenue_export.csv is a sample. Build a reusable petl report: in examples/revenue_report.py define net_revenue(input_path, output_path, rejects_path), and add a CLI, examples/revenue_report_cli.py, that takes the input, output, and rejects paths as positional arguments and calls net_revenue. Input rules: UTF-8 CSV that may start with a byte-order mark; the region and amount columns can appear in any position among other columns. An amount is an optional minus sign or enclosing parentheses (a refund, so (12.00) means -12.00), an optional $ after the sign or opening parenthesis, digits with optional comma thousands separators, and an optional decimal fraction, with surrounding whitespace allowed; anything else, including an empty value, n/a, or 1e3, is unparseable. Trim regions and group them case-insensitively. A data row whose region is blank or whose amount is unparseable is excluded from totals and written to rejects_path as CSV with header row,region,amount: row is its 1-based data-row number (the header is not counted), region and amount are the raw values as read, and rejects stay in input order. Write output_path as CSV with header region,net: one row per region in upper case, sorted, with net the exact Decimal sum rounded half away from zero to two decimal places. Never use floats for money, and do not fetch anything. Run a focused check.
